keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B minor is the relative minor of D major

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Minor tonic establishing the quirky, deadpan verse storytelling
D (bIII / Relative I) - Relative major tonic brightening the first beat of every chorus line
A (bVII) - Subtonic chord providing constant rhythmic bounce back to Bm or D
G (bVI) - Submediant chord pairing with A for the classic bVI-bVII turnaround at the end of every two-bar phrase

techniques.name: Reggae-Pop Offbeat Skank & Relative Major Chorus Lift
techniques.description: Tight, staccato offbeat barre-chord chops in the verse paired with open, ringing power/open chords in the chorus

sequence: Mute strings on the downbeats (1, 2, 3, 4) and strike crisp upstrokes on the '&' of beats during the verse
Release fretting-hand pressure immediately after each upstroke to get a dry, percussive chop
Switch the first chord of the loop from Bm to open D major when the chorus hits
Play the G to A turnaround on beats 3 and 4 of every second bar
tips: For the verse reggae chop, use compact 3- or 4-string barre shapes on the top strings so every chord cuts cleanly
Count '1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &' out loud and accent the '&' syllables to lock into Colin Hay's rhythm
In the chorus, let the open D major chord ring out fully to contrast with the clipped verse

sections.name: Verse Reggae Skank
sections.description: Clipped, bouncy offbeat chords over the two-bar Bm - A - Bm - G - A groove.
notes: Focus on the upper four strings for a bright, reggae-influenced chop
Release finger pressure right after striking to stop the chord from ringing
Nail the quick G to A change in the second bar

sections.name: Chorus ('Land Down Under')
sections.description: Substituting D major for the first Bm chord transforms the minor verse loop into an unforgettable major-key anthem.
notes: Hit the open D major chord strongly on beat 1 of bar 1
Notice how bars 1 and 2 still end with the exact same G to A turnaround
Keep the 107 BPM groove buoyant and relaxed

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.technique: B Minor Flute Hook on Guitar
sections.description: Greg Ham's iconic B minor flute riff transcribed for single-note lead guitar in 7th position.
notes: Play in 7th position (index finger on fret 7)
Use crisp staccato articulation to mimic the flute phrasing
Target the root B on the 4th string 9th fret and 1st string 7th fret

guitar.recommended: Fender Telecaster or Fender Stratocaster (Colin Hay & Ron Strykert)
alternatives: Maton Acoustic (for Colin Hay unplugged style)
guitar.pickup: Bridge and middle single-coil combination for snappy new-wave cluck

amp.recommended: Roland JC-120 or Fender Twin Reverb

settings.bass: 4 (low cut so bass guitar dominates the bottom end)

effects.distortion: Light overdrive on chorus power chords
effects.delay: Short slapback or quarter-note dub echo
effects.other: Compressor pedal for even, percussive upstroke volume

beginner.title: Four-Chord Loop & Simplified Bm
steps: Learn D, A, G, and the 4-string Bm triad (X-X-4-4-3-2)
Practice the two-bar verse loop (Bm - A | Bm - G - A) with simple downstrokes
Switch the first Bm to D major for the chorus
Play through the full song at 107 BPM

intermediate.title: Reggae Upstroke Skank & Full Barre Chords
steps: Master the full 5-string Bm barre chord (X-2-4-4-3-2)
Play the verse using muted downbeats and staccato upstrokes on the '&' counts
Learn the B minor flute melody on the upper strings

advanced.title: Loop-Pedal Arrangement (Rhythm + Flute Lead)
steps: Lay down the reggae rhythm loop and perform the flute hook live over the top
Incorporate Ron Strykert's syncopated single-note muted funk-reggae lines
Perform Colin Hay's dynamic solo-acoustic storytelling arrangement

commonMistakes: Strumming heavy on beats 1 and 3 in the verse instead of accenting the offbeats
Forgetting that the second bar of every phrase has a faster harmonic rhythm (Bm for 2 beats, then G and A for 1 beat each)
Failing to mute the low E string on the Bm barre chord
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: Bm → A → G chord transition drill
4 minutes: Offbeat upstroke skank exercise with fretting-hand muting at 90 BPM
4 minutes: Flute hook lead melody practice in 7th position
4 minutes: Full song playthrough at 107 BPM
focusAreas: Crisp fretting-hand muting for reggae upstrokes
Seamless switch between the B minor verse and D major chorus
Accurate timing on the G-A bar-2 turnaround
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 90 BPM and treat clicks as beats 2 and 4
Bring tempo up to 107 BPM while keeping upstrokes razor-sharp
Practice transitioning between the rhythm skank and the single-note flute lead
